THE INVESTIGATOR’S HANDBOOK

Digital Crime Investigation

Benild Joseph
SYLLABUS READING GUIDE

Digital Crime Investigation

Benild Joseph

2017 · Independent publication

A compact introduction to internet crime, online evidence, IP tracing, email attacks, phishing, and the Indian legal context at the time of publication.

Publisher’s editionPrint guide
A public, complete publisher chapter listing was not verified. The eight sections below are an original thematic reading route, not a claimed exact table of contents. Match them to the headings in your copy and replace pre-2024 legal references.
READ WITH A QUESTION IN MIND

Your chapter connections.

8 study sections
01

Study route 1 · Conventional and cybercrime

Identify how familiar offences acquire a digital component and define the conduct precisely.

1.4 · Criminalization of Conduct in Cyberspace1.5 · Types of Internet Crimes and Cyber Offences
02

Study route 2 · The range of cyber offences and actors

Separate roles, capabilities, and motivations from the legal elements of an offence.

1.5 · Types of Internet Crimes and Cyber Offences5.1 · Introduction to Cyber Threat Intelligence
03

Study route 3 · Web-based email attacks and phishing

Practise header interpretation, message preservation, and independent payment verification.

3.11 · Email Forensics
04

Study route 4 · Collecting and documenting online evidence

Build a source, capture, integrity, and custody record that another examiner can follow.

2.6 · Collection and Preservation of Digital Evidence2.8 · Chain of Custody in Digital Investigations2.11 · Documentation and Reporting of Digital Evidence
05

Study route 5 · IP addresses and online tracing

Understand what an address can show, and where NAT, proxies, and provider records limit attribution.

2.5 · Sources of Electronic Evidence3.9 · Network Forensics
06

Study route 6 · The forensic toolkit

Choose tools for acquisition and examination, and record versions, settings, and limitations.

4.1 · Introduction to Digital Evidence Forensic Toolkit (DEFT)4.2 · Introduction to Kali Linux Environment4.3 · Installation and Configuration of DEFT
07

Study route 7 · Indian cybercrime law and intermediaries

Read the historical discussion alongside the current IT Rules and the BNS, BNSS, and BSA. Do not reuse old section numbers automatically.

1.6 · Overview of Information Technology Act and Cyber Laws1.7 · Comparison of IPC/CrPC/Evidence Act with BNS/BNSS/BSA1.10 · Information Technology Rules, 2018
08

Study route 8 · From investigation to presentation

Connect technical findings to a clear report and the applicable electronic-evidence certification process.

2.10 · Section 63(4) BSA and Electronic Evidence Certification4.9 · Preparation of Forensic Reports4.12 · Courtroom Presentation and Expert Testimony
